findings.title: One reported gift changes the September story
findings.answer: September 1–27 reports $20,056,194.92 in cash contributions. Transaction 5816290—the $10 million Carpenters contribution to Building a Stronger Oregon—is 49.9% of that total. Excluding that one record leaves $10,056,194.92, versus $13,697,269.57 in the full month of August.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: All September 1–27 cash-contribution rows: 11,378; denominator 2005619492 cents.
findings.calculation: Single-record influence analysis: subtract the specified transaction from the September sum, retaining every other row and the same accounting basis.
findings.whyItMatters: An aggregate fundraising surge can reflect a single institutional funding event rather than a broad-based increase in participation.
findings.uncertainty: September is incomplete, reporting can arrive later, and the comparison is not seasonally adjusted. No claim about acceleration, spending, donor intent or electoral effect.
findings.competingExplanations: Other campaigns can accelerate even when an aggregate comparison is dominated by one receipt. Gross receipts still include committee transfers.

findings.title: Similar 2026 fundraising masks sharply different reported cash positions
findings.answer: Kotek’s committee reports $10,293,083.12 in 2026 cash contributions and Drazan’s $9,764,922.48. Their retrieved official summaries report closing cash of $8,376,671.93 and $964,650.50, respectively—a 8.68-to-one ratio.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: Two authoritative committees, 4792 and 19050; official 2026 account summaries retrieved September 27. A selected comparison, not a ranking of all candidates.
findings.calculation: Reconcile official opening cash + official net change = closing cash. Compare same-year contribution and payment bases; do not infer balances from receipts alone.
findings.whyItMatters: Kotek started 2026 with $2,432,342.22 and reports $4,353,542.97 in cash expenditures. Drazan started with $982,810.75 and reports $9,774,591.62. Both starting resources and spending distinguish their positions.
findings.uncertainty: These are reported—not bank-verified—balances. Drazan’s official cash payments exceed the fixed snapshot by $800.00; that unresolved difference is retained. Cash balances do not measure unpaid commitments, campaign quality or election probability.
findings.competingExplanations: Earlier spending may already have purchased advertising, organization or other useful capacity. A lower balance is not itself a weaker campaign or proof of poor management.

findings.title: Public matching is the majority of reported cash for all 13 linked certified candidates
findings.answer: Classified matching-fund receipts supply 66.1% of the combined $2,062,510.81 in cash contributions reported by the 13 linked Portland certified candidates. Every one of the 13 is above half; individual shares range from 50.9% to 82.4%.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: These 13 committees’ cash contributions across January 1, 2025–September 27, 2026: 206251081 cents. Reviewed matching receipt numerator: 136371300 cents.
findings.calculation: Sum reviewed public matching receipt classifications and divide by the same committees’ reported cash contributions. Do not add City distribution totals to committee receipts.
findings.whyItMatters: In this group, a gross fundraising ranking is substantially a public-financing ranking. It cannot be read as a ranking of private fundraising alone.
findings.uncertainty: Not all Portland candidates, not a causal comparison of participants with nonparticipants, and not an exact City disbursement-level match. Unclassified receipts are not certified private money.
findings.competingExplanations: The City and fixed ORESTAR observations differ in timing and coverage. Public matching may reflect qualifying participation, but these totals alone do not establish broader or more representative donor support.

findings.title: Reported resources are not one additive pot
findings.answer: Cash contributions total $121,794,170.02; cash payments total $91,270,955.55. Loans, in-kind support, refunds and obligations remain separate.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: All current rows in each explicitly defined financial basis; 316,926 rows overall.
findings.calculation: Sum exact integer-cent Amount within each subtype/basis; never add Aggregate Amount.
findings.whyItMatters: This prevents circulation, debt and later settlement from masquerading as new purchasing power.
findings.uncertainty: Not outside-money totals, complete cycles, bank balances or an audit of whether filings are accurate.
findings.competingExplanations: A large expenditure can be a transfer, reimbursement or pass-through rather than a vendor earning.

findings.title: The three largest recipients span different political roles
findings.answer: Friends of Tina Kotek, Friends of Christine Drazan and Building a Stronger Oregon report $34,383,392.21 combined cash contributions (28.2% of reported cash). A single September 16, 2026 Carpenters contribution to Building a Stronger Oregon is $10 million.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.calculation: Order committee-own cash receipts; sum first three. Named committee type/candidate associations reviewed against official profiles.
findings.whyItMatters: Magnitude is concentrated, but a PAC is not equivalent to a candidate campaign in a same-race comparison.
findings.uncertainty: No conclusion about ultimate spending, obligations to a contributor or purchased influence.
findings.competingExplanations: Election stage, incumbent committees, PAC roles and pre-period resources make a pooled ranking an imperfect comparison.

findings.title: Concentration survives several accounting and identity scenarios
findings.answer: Visible-source Gini is 0.905; removing the largest group leaves 0.896. Aggressive same-name/type grouping yields 0.913. Top-ten visible-source share is 21.5%, falling to 14.7% after removing the largest group.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: 54,551 positive visible source groups; $109,772,183.24. Includes committee sources; excludes disclosure/unknown groups.
findings.calculation: Gini, HHI, effective groups and top shares over positive cumulative group amounts. Separate committee-source exclusion and individual-only scenarios.
findings.whyItMatters: Unevenness is not solely an artifact of the single largest visible source, although its influence is substantial.
findings.uncertainty: Fingerprints are provisional. Sensitivity grouping is intentionally aggressive and is not an identity decision. Hidden activity remains unallocated.
findings.competingExplanations: Public funding and committee transfers differ from private individual giving, so the source population changes the substantive interpretation.

findings.title: Most small transactions supply a small share of visible dollars
findings.answer: Transactions of $100 or less are 69.5% of nonaggregate cash rows but 3.1% of their dollars. Transactions over $1,000 are 4.9% of these rows and 81.7% of their dollars.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: 178,496 cash-contribution rows after excluding aggregate categories; 10977218324 cents.
findings.calculation: Mutually exclusive transaction-size bands; compare record share and dollar share. Cumulative source totals are separate.
findings.whyItMatters: Transaction volume and financial weight tell different stories; neither counts unique people.
findings.uncertainty: Small gifts are not necessarily small cumulative donors. Prior unitemized giving is not recoverable.
findings.competingExplanations: Recurring giving raises the count of small transactions without increasing the number of identified sources.

findings.title: Disclosure categories count money but cannot count people
findings.answer: 32,258 contribution-family rows total $12,084,155.64 under miscellaneous or anonymous labels.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: All 217,239 contribution-family records, across contribution subtypes; not solely cash.
findings.calculation: Explicit label rules create committee-scoped disclosure buckets, excluded from identity graphs.
findings.whyItMatters: Treating the same aggregate label as a donor would fabricate ties across unrelated committees.
findings.uncertainty: No full distinct-person count or cross-campaign donor attribution is identifiable for those amounts.
findings.competingExplanations: Aggregate reporting can be normal under disclosure rules; visibility gaps are not automatically violations.

findings.title: The strict transfer count is deliberately conservative
findings.answer: 1,454 strict same-day pairs total $7,796,853.20. A maximum one-to-one reconciliation within seven-day candidates can match $17,927,165.51 across 3,847 pairs.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: Cash receipt/payment pairs with reciprocal authoritative committee IDs, equal positive cents and dates within seven days.
findings.calculation: Maximum one-to-one bipartite matching across all reciprocal-ID, equal-amount, seven-day candidate pairs. Both sides retained.
findings.whyItMatters: Internal circulation is sensitive to matching rules; neither side of a paired transfer is a new external dollar.
findings.uncertainty: Maximum is a possible reconciliation within this candidate set, not a verified transfer total or a global upper bound on all internal transfers. One optimum may not be unique; unmatched transfers may have changed dates/amounts or missing IDs.
findings.competingExplanations: An ordinary $1,208,352.82 nurses’ PAC payment and next-day receipt fail the strict same-day test without implying misconduct.

findings.title: Reported location is not district residency
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: All cash-contribution cents including unknown-state rows: 12179417002.
findings.calculation: Reported State equals OR, another code, or blank. Unknown remains in denominator.
findings.whyItMatters: An outside-Oregon comparison is available now; a neighborhood-representation claim needs boundaries and population denominators.
findings.uncertainty: No geocoded legal residence or district membership; aggregate records concentrate in unknown locations.
findings.competingExplanations: Employer/business mailing locations can differ from residence, and committees can have statewide constituencies.

findings.title: Portland’s two funding records overlap and differ
findings.answer: The City reports $1,542,435.00 distributed to 13 certified candidates. Reviewed matching receipts in the fixed snapshot total $1,363,713.00; the difference is $178,722.00.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: Thirteen certified 2026 Portland program candidates, linked to authoritative ORESTAR committees; source observations retrieved September 27.
findings.calculation: Compare City cumulative amount with classified ORESTAR receipts by reviewed committee. Do not combine the two sources.
findings.whyItMatters: Public matching must be distinguished from private giving before comparing campaign dependency or breadth.
findings.uncertainty: Aggregate reconciliation only, not City payment-level matching. The unclassified remainder is not verified private money.
findings.competingExplanations: Reporting timing, late filings, amendments and differing source coverage can explain differences. No allegation is made.

findings.title: Balances require a starting point and an explicit reconciliation
findings.answer: Among 41 retrieved committee-year summaries, 39 agree with snapshot cash contributions, payments and net change; 2 retain discrepancies.
findings.population: Fixed ORESTAR current-version snapshot; any narrower population is specified in the denominator.
findings.denominator: Targeted 25 of 1,888 filers, not a representative sample.
findings.calculation: Check official opening + official net = closing, adjacent-year roll-forward, and source-basis ledger reconciliation.
findings.whyItMatters: Reported flows alone cannot establish reserves, outstanding debt or runway.
findings.uncertainty: Official summaries are live observations, not independently audited bank statements. Statewide coverage remains incomplete.
findings.competingExplanations: Different retrieval times, future-dated records or amendments can create disagreement with an immutable snapshot.
